prompt:
Use case: photorealistic-natural
Asset type: RGBA tree foliage atlas for distant vegetation in a realistic Tuscan hill-town game.
Primary request: one square transparent image containing exactly four separate full-tree photographic cutouts in a strict equal 2 by 2 grid. Top left: broad irregular mature holm oak. Top right: taller deciduous oak with a broken asymmetrical crown. Bottom left: a low wide Mediterranean olive tree. Bottom right: dense rounded but irregular evergreen holm oak with a slightly different branching silhouette.
Composition: each entire tree fits alone inside its quadrant with at least 6 percent transparent margin on every side of that quadrant; centered horizontally, base of trunk near the bottom of its quadrant. No tree crosses a quadrant boundary. Front elevation at canopy height, orthographic appearance, no visible ground. Each crown occupies most of its width, with visible fine leaf sprays and irregular gaps. Natural, believable tree proportions, modest exposed trunks.
Style: realistic vegetation photography, fine individually resolved leaves and twigs; sophisticated natural olive and deep green tones. Soft neutral daylight, readable layered foliage and gentle self-shadow; no hard directional cast shadows.
Background: genuine transparent alpha everywhere outside the trees, including gaps between leaves and branches. No ground shadow, no sky, no horizon, no soil, no border, no labels, no text, no grid lines, no checkerboard baked into the image. Preserve delicate leaf edges in the alpha. Avoid stylized blobs and geometric spherical crowns.
